title: Adaptive multi-metric A/B controller with exposure scheduling and auto-rollback
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Engineering teams running model rollouts need a predictable, auditable A/B controller that can schedule exposure, enforce multi-metric safety gates, perform sequential statistical checks, and trigger automated rollback when regressions are detected. Current rollout primitives are either too manual (scripts + dashboards) or only single-metric driven, which leads to missed cross-metric regressions.

Goal: Deliver an 'A/B Controller' service and Console UX that lets PMs/ML engineers define experiments for model versions with: composite metric definitions (direction + weight), exposure ramps (time-based or event-based), configurable statistical tests (sequential testing, optional Bayesian alternative), and automated rollback actions wired into the serving runtime. The solution should be observable, auditable, and support staged deployments (shadow -> canary -> full).
acceptance_criteria: Composite metric editor in Console: define metrics, direction (increase/decrease), weight, and thresholds for pass/fail.
Exposure scheduler: create ramps (e.g., 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) with halt-on-guardrail option.
Statistical engine: sequential testing with alpha spending, minimum sample enforcement, and per-metric significance reporting.
Auto-rollback: when pre-defined composite score or any critical metric hits configured fail condition, controller triggers rollout rollback and alerts SRE and owners.
Runtime integration: routing policy can accept controller decisions and immediately change variant exposure without redeploy.
Observability: experiment dashboard with variant time-series, p-values, confidence intervals, sample counts, and links to raw logs/requests.
E2E tests and canary run completed in staging with at least one internal experiment and no false positive rollbacks in load tests.
implementation_notes: 2026-02-05 Design review with Eng, SRE, and Research: agreed on sequential frequentist approach for first MVP due to interpretability and lower compute footprint; Bayesian option left as follow-up.
Trade-offs: sequential frequentist tests require alpha-spending correction and conservative thresholds to avoid premature rollbacks under nonstationary traffic; we prioritized safety over early wins.

Architecture: controller service exposes REST + gRPC API. Runtime polls controller decisions and supports traffic shaping via weight updates. Controller maintains experiment state, computes statistics from aggregated event streams (metric service), and emits actions (pause, continue, rollback).
Data pipeline: metrics aggregated through Metrics Ingest (ENG-4123). Minimum sample size checks implemented in the controller to avoid underpowered decisions.
Prototype: feature-branch for controller and metric aggregation in github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/experiments/pull/4123
Staging results: 2026-03-02 load run with synthetic traffic simulating 5% noise; controller maintained correct p-value accumulation and did not trigger rollback when within thresholds.
Next steps: wire Console rollout UI (Console ticket: PM-11345), add audit log entries per decision (security review required), and build canary templates for common ramp patterns.
Owner: Diego Morales (PM) coordinates release and runbook; Eng lead: Priya Shah; SRE: Marcus Lee.
